tools.title: Vox
tools.pitch: Offline dictation — hold a key, talk, and cleaned-up text lands in whatever window has focus.
tools.audience: For writers and devs who talk faster than they type and won't install cloud dictation.

tools.title: pomodoro-timer
tools.pitch: A desktop pomodoro timer that stays out of the way — tray-native, no account, no sync.
tools.audience: For desk workers who want a timer, not a productivity platform.

tools.title: Senses
tools.pitch: Modular AR audio-visual instruments for Android — camera, motion, and generative audio composed into playable artifacts.
tools.audience: For performers and visual artists who want the room itself to become the instrument.

tools.title: Assay
tools.pitch: A dataset investigation workbench — from a raw download to verified findings.
tools.audience: For people who investigate datasets instead of just downloading them.

tools.title: studytool
tools.pitch: Spaced-repetition flashcards for Android — drop in an Anki deck and study offline. No account, no sync, no server.
tools.audience: For students who want Anki's rigor on a phone without Anki's friction.

tools.title: Vox for Android
tools.pitch: On-device dictation — a floating mic bubble, local whisper transcription, LLM cleanup, and the text lands wherever your cursor is.
tools.audience: For phone typists who'd rather talk — without a cloud listening.

tools.title: juniper
tools.pitch: A personal voice assistant for Android — on-device wake word and speech, Claude for the thinking, every word captured to your Obsidian vault before it's answered.
tools.audience: For people who want an assistant that writes everything down and keeps it theirs.
